newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CHASTENED AUSTRALIAN DLR QUIETENS AFTER REBUFF.
newsitem.headline: CHASTENED AUSTRALIAN DLR QUIETENS AFTER REBUFF.

text.p: A suitably chastened Australian dollar quietened down after a late morning attempt to breach US$0.7400 produced a strong rebuttal that knocked the dollar down by a quarter of a cent.
Despite the knockback, the dollar managed to hold on to its overnight gains, and has now established a comfortable buffer above the two year low under US$0.7300 it reached last week.

Late in the session, as the Europeans entered, the dollar ticked up again and by 4.45 p.m. (0645 GMT) it was was trading at US0.7391/96, up from an early US$0.7383/88 and a sizeable margin above Monday's local close of US$0.7362/67.

Shortcovering and some local buying had seen the dollar rise to US$0.7405, its highest level in a week, in late morning trade. However the unit was swamped by sellers, mainly from Asia, that saw it drop to its lows for the day at US$0.7379.

While the market is waiting on a speech from Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Ian Macfarlane later today, traders said the dollar was likely to range trade in the near term as the interest rate outlook remained uncertain.
"We're in a range, US$0.7300 on the bottom, US$0.7420 on the top, or even US$0.7450," one trader said.
"We will consolidate in a range for a while, until we get some more data and that could be a couple of weeks," he said.
News of a 0.2 percent rise in June manufacturing output prices had little effect on the market, which has become used to figures showing an absence of inflation pressures.
Macfarlane is the after dinner speaker at a Perth function, with a topic of "Monetary Policy and Growth." He is expected to start talking around 11.00 p.m. Sydney time (1300 GMT).
It is his first speech since the July 30 rate cut, and his first speech in Australia since before the May 23 rate cut, and the market will be searching for clues to the rate outlook.

It is also the first RBA appearance since the July announcement that the RBA had sold two thirds of its gold reserves. Perth is the capital of Western Australia, which produces about 70 percent of Australia's gold.

Generally, the speech is expected to be favourable for the dollar, as Macfarlane is seen suggesting that while inflation is under control the RBA is waiting for the impact of the five rate cuts delivered since July last year to come through.
"We expect that Macfarlane will be pleased with the prices and wages outlook, and also to express confidence about the growth outlook," Bankers Trust economist John Horner said.
On the crosses, the dollar held on to overnight gains that were the result of a recovery in the U.S. dollar.
The dollar finished at 85.81/91 yen and 1.3777/90 marks from an early 85.74/84 and 1.3754/67 and a local close on Monday of 84.72/82 and 1.3588/3605.
In trade weighted terms the dollar was steady through the day at 58.1, after rising overnight from Monday's 57.6 close.
There was potential for the U.S. dollar, and with it the Australian dollar, to strengthen further against the mark after the German Bundesbank left the repo rate unchanged on Tuesday.
